drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment

Evidence includes 'innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data', 'develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs', and 'provides specialized expertise and consultative services regarding production systems and processes'. This is stronger than narrower processing subprocesses because the work spans the end-to-end production architecture, partner coordination, schedules, and system specifications. Future drivers such as enterprise digital platforms, integrated data pipelines, modular architecture, AI/automation, and workforce transition would most directly change this role by shifting it toward reusable enterprise workflows, orchestration, cloud/platform-based production, and redesigned staff-system interactions.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: AI and automation have a major impact on production system and workflow design because they shift statistical production toward integrated, monitored, reusable, and automated enterprise workflows with clearer handoffs, fewer manual interventions, and new human-in-the-loop roles.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Production workflows are materially redesigned to support ingestion, linkage, monitoring and processing of multiple non-survey sources alongside online collection. This includes integrating SDLE-enabled linkage flows, supplier-driven refresh cycles, geospatial inputs, and adaptive collection triggers. Workforce impacts are direct because roles, handoffs and system interactions change across collection, analysis and dissemination teams.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline
drivers.impact: Execution discipline materially affects workflow design because production systems must be structured for timely delivery, clear handoffs, explicit accountabilities, and minimal bottlenecks. Workflow design becomes more milestone-driven and operationally governed to support faster implementation and active management of deadlines.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: This subprocess is heavily affected because end-to-end workflows, system interactions and business architecture must be redesigned to embed secure access, authorization, privacy controls and resilience across the production chain. It is a central point where secure modernization of platforms and reusable services is operationalized.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: This subprocess is directly and heavily affected because the driver is fundamentally about enterprise platforms, cloud environments, tooling and architecture. Production workflows must be redesigned around reusable enterprise services, cloud-hosted components, secure access models, integrated repositories and staff interaction with modern platforms.

drivers.driver: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline
drivers.impact: Governance reform materially affects workflow and production-system design by imposing clearer enterprise decision rights, stronger reuse expectations, explicit prioritization of design choices, and clearer assignment of responsibilities across teams. This changes both the target workflow and the operating model embedded in it.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: This subprocess is directly transformed by the driver because the core design task becomes creating integrated, orchestrated end-to-end workflows that connect collection, processing, analysis and dissemination with minimal manual breaks.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because metadata-driven data management requires workflows and production systems to treat metadata as a core enterprise asset across the end-to-end process. Workflow design must support metadata capture, storage, linkage, discoverability and reuse across systems.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: Next-generation production directly transforms workflow and system design toward enterprise, metadata-driven, cloud-enabled, reusable production architectures. This subprocess must redesign end-to-end workflows to reduce manual handoffs, support integrated pipelines, and align staff roles with modern platforms and automation.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: This subprocess is one of the most directly affected because the driver is fundamentally about designing production around modular architecture, microservices, reusable enterprise components, and self-service development under guardrails. Workflow design must explicitly prioritize reuse, interoperability, governance, supportability, and staff operating models.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: This subprocess is central to the driver because it redesigns end-to-end workflows for efficiency, reuse, fewer handoffs, flatter decision paths, and reduced staffing intensity across production.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: This subprocess is directly and significantly affected because the driver is fundamentally about how staff, managers, and leaders operate in modernized workflows. impacts.justification: Configure workflows is the second strongest fit because the role moves beyond design into implementation of new or modified processing systems and maintenance of operational production flows. Evidence includes 'occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems', 'establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams', and 'coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules'. This is stronger than pure build of individual components because the work emphasizes operational configuration, parameters, schedules, handoffs and coordinated execution across teams. Future drivers around integrated process orchestration, execution discipline, secure workflow controls, and efficiency pressures will likely increase the need for workflow configuration, monitoring, exception handling and standardized reusable flows.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is directly and significantly affected because AI and automation are embedded into operational pipelines, requiring orchestration of automated tasks, monitoring, exception handling, and standardized handoffs across collection, processing, analysis, and dissemination.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because operational flows must be configured for recurring administrative feeds, linkage steps, online-first collection paths, adaptive follow-up logic, and geospatial processing. This changes orchestration across collection, processing and dissemination and requires staff to work within more automated, source-driven workflows.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because execution discipline must be translated into operational workflow configurations that support milestone tracking, timely sequencing, and rapid implementation. Configuration choices need to reduce friction and enable active management of delivery against deadlines.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because security controls, access rules and resilient operating patterns must be implemented in the actual orchestration of end-to-end processes. Standard workflows need secure configuration rather than only functional assembly.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is strongly affected because enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure determine how end-to-end statistical workflows are assembled, automated, secured and monitored. Standardized enterprise workflows become more feasible and more necessary.

drivers.driver: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because stronger governance and decision discipline constrain how far teams can customize workflows, reinforce enterprise-standard configurations, and require clearer approval and accountability for deviations and resource use.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: This is one of the most directly affected subprocesses because the driver centers on configuring orchestrated end-to-end workflows, automated triggers, dependencies, and handoffs across the production chain.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because metadata capture, propagation, linkage and publication must be configured across the end-to-end process. Metadata handling becomes part of operational workflow orchestration rather than a separate documentation activity.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because next-generation production depends on assembling automated, integrated, metadata-driven flows across collection, processing, and dissemination. Legacy manual sequences are replaced or reduced through enterprise orchestration and standardized reusable configurations.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is directly affected because modular architecture and self-service development move implementation toward assembling standard workflow patterns, reusable services, and configurable transformations rather than coding bespoke end-to-end flows.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because efficiency targets require standardized, automated, and simplified operational flows with fewer manual checkpoints and less management overhead.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because modernization requires operationalizing new ways of working in systems while ensuring staff and managers can execute them. Configuration choices must align with workforce skills, leadership accountabilities, and realistic workload sequencing.

impacts.justification: Review and validate is the third strongest relationship because validation and quality assurance are a recurring operational responsibility in the work description. Evidence includes 'coordinates activities ... to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data', 'develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs', 'devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies', and 'research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems'. This is stronger than adjacent subprocesses such as edit/impute or finalise data files because the description emphasizes validation rules, inconsistency detection, acceptance criteria and output quality more directly than data correction. Future-state drivers such as AI and automation, alternative and integrated data, metadata-driven processing, and reduced staffing will likely shift this work toward more automated validation, exception-based review, and stronger quality governance for complex multi-source outputs.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Review and validation are strongly affected because AI and automation enable more continuous, rules-based and model-assisted detection of anomalies and errors, while increasing the need for monitoring, human oversight, and transparent validation logic.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Validation is strongly affected because heterogeneous administrative, alternative and linked sources introduce new risks: duplicates, linkage errors, inconsistent concepts, source drift, missing metadata and structural anomalies. Validation must increasingly operate across sources and after integration, not just within a single survey dataset.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Validation is materially affected because modern platforms and cloud-based processing environments enable more scalable and standardized validation workflows, while secure access and data protection controls shape who can inspect sensitive records and where validation can occur.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Validation is materially affected because orchestrated pipelines require validation steps to run automatically at defined points, generate machine-actionable outcomes, and support exception routing across the end-to-end flow.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Validation is materially affected because metadata-driven processing provides clearer definitions, structures and expected values against which data can be checked. Metadata quality itself also becomes part of what must be validated for downstream reuse.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: Validation is materially affected because modernized production introduces more heterogeneous sources, linkage-based inputs, and automated methods that require stronger, more scalable validation rules and monitoring. Validation also becomes more iterative and automated to support timelier outputs and reduced manual intervention.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: Validation is directly and significantly affected because the driver explicitly emphasizes validation in environments built from reusable components, open-source tools, and self-service development. Standardised, reusable validation rules and controls become essential to maintain trust and production reliability.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Validation processes are materially affected as organizations seek more automated error detection, prioritization, and exception handling to maintain quality with fewer staff.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: Review and validation are materially affected because modernized production introduces new tools, AI-assisted checks, and more complex data sources, requiring upgraded staff capability and management oversight to maintain quality.

impacts.justification: The strongest relationship is with Integrate data because the role explicitly centers on 'data integration, data manipulation' and 'technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources'. This is stronger than analysis or dissemination subprocesses because integration and linkage are named core responsibilities, not just adjacent tasks. Future drivers such as administrative, alternative and linked data expansion, metadata-driven interoperability, enterprise platforms, and integrated pipelines will directly reshape this role toward more complex multi-source harmonisation, reusable linkage environments, and stronger governance of integrated data assets.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: AI and automation materially affect data integration by enabling more automated ingestion and harmonisation of diverse structured and unstructured sources, while increasing the need for governed, secure, and monitored integration pipelines.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: This is one of the most directly affected subprocesses. The driver explicitly expands the use of administrative, alternative, linked and geospatial data, making integration, harmonisation, prioritisation and record linkage central production activities. SDLE-enabled linkage and multi-source consolidation become core to replacing or supplementing survey inputs and improving timeliness and relevance.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Data integration is one of the most materially affected subprocesses because linking and combining sources increases privacy, confidentiality and cyber risk. drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Data integration is strongly affected because enterprise data platforms, centralized repositories and cloud infrastructure materially improve the ability to combine, harmonize and manage multiple sources at scale. drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Data integration is a core impact area because integrated pipelines make source combination, sequencing, and automated movement of consolidated data central to the operating model.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: This subprocess is one of the most directly affected because metadata-driven management improves interoperability and reuse across sources. Standardized metadata materially changes how sources are matched, harmonised, prioritised and integrated.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: Data integration is one of the most directly affected subprocesses because next-generation production relies on combining survey, administrative, alternative, geospatial, and linked data sources in reusable enterprise pipelines. drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: Data integration is materially affected because modular architectures and interoperable services change how data from multiple sources are connected, harmonised, and reused across processes. Integration logic is more likely to be implemented through shared services and standard interfaces.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: As cost pressures encourage substitution of direct collection with existing sources, data integration becomes more central and more operationally important for sustaining outputs efficiently.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: Data integration is materially affected because modernization increases use of new data sources and more complex integration methods, which require stronger analytical expertise, updated technical skills, and careful sequencing of work under constrained staffing.

impacts.justification: Derive new variables and units is the second strongest fit because the role performs 'data analytics and in-depth analysis' and develops initiatives for 'new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing ... data'. Those responsibilities imply transforming integrated data into analytic constructs and model-based outputs, especially when alternative data sources and linkage are involved. This is stronger than aggregate calculation because the description emphasizes modeling and analytic transformation rather than only summarizing data. Future drivers around modern statistical methods, linked data, and automation will likely increase the derivation of analytical variables and units from combined administrative, alternative and linked sources.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: AI and automation materially affect derivation by enabling more automated and model-assisted creation of derived variables and units, especially where complex transformations are embedded in repeatable production workflows.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: This subprocess is materially affected because linked and administrative data expansion increases reliance on deriving statistical variables and units from existing records rather than collecting them directly. It also supports deriving households, enterprises, spatial indicators and other analytical constructs from linked person, business and geospatial sources.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Derivation is materially affected because integrated pipelines and orchestration require explicit dependency management and automated execution order for derived variables and units.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Derivation is materially affected because metadata-driven management requires derived variables and units to be documented in standardized ways so they can be understood, discovered and reused. This strengthens lineage and semantic clarity for downstream users.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: This subprocess is affected where efficiency strategies replace direct collection with derivation from existing data, increasing reliance on automated derivation logic and model-based methods.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: Derivation of variables and units is materially affected because modernization expands the use of advanced methods and analytical tools, increasing the need for staff capability in model-based derivation and careful sequencing of technical work.

impacts.justification: Produce dissemination products is the third strongest relationship because the role explicitly produces 'dissemination and data visualization products' and supports new methods for disseminating data to meet user needs. This is stronger than 6.1 Prepare draft outputs because the description points to actual production of dissemination and visualization products rather than only draft analytical material. Future drivers such as metadata-driven discoverability, enterprise digital platforms, automation, and modular dissemination tools will likely change this work toward more standardized, reusable, digitally enabled products with richer metadata and self-service features.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Production of dissemination products is materially affected because automation can assemble standard products faster and AI can support drafting and user-facing features, while transparency and trust require stronger quality statements and explanatory content.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Dissemination products are materially affected because the driver enables more products based on linked, administrative and geospatial data, including maps and linked open data, while also requiring stronger quality statements and methodological explanation. drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Production of dissemination products is materially affected because digital products must be assembled in ways that preserve privacy and support secure release, especially for interactive products, downloadable files and public-use microdata.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Production of dissemination products is materially affected because enterprise digital platforms and cloud services support more scalable, reusable and interactive digital products, while secure tooling and privacy controls shape how products are assembled and prepared for release.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Production of dissemination products is affected where recurring product assembly can be fed and partially automated by orchestrated upstream pipelines, reducing manual compilation of standard outputs.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration

impacts.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the position explicitly analyzes user requirements from other national statistical offices and multilateral organizations in order to determine the most appropriate research, comparative analysis studies, sources of information, methods and approaches. That aligns with establishing output objectives by shaping what will be delivered, to whom, on what timeline and with what resources. This is slightly weaker than 1.1 because user need identification is more explicit and foundational in the work description, but stronger than most other subprocesses because the analyst materially influences scope, priorities and deliverables. Future drivers around governance, prioritization and efficiency are likely to change this work by forcing clearer enterprise decisions about international commitments, service levels, and trade-offs among scope, timeliness and internal capacity.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline
drivers.impact: Testing is materially affected because fixed delivery dates compress testing windows and increase the need for disciplined sign-off, prioritised defect resolution, and risk-based readiness decisions. The subprocess must balance speed with stewardship and delivery assurance.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Testing is strongly affected because secure channels, access controls, privacy protections and resilience must be validated before production use. Security and privacy assurance become part of system sign-off, not just functional testing.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Testing production systems is materially affected because cloud-hosted, platform-based and security-sensitive environments require more extensive integration, performance, access-control and secure transmission testing across reusable enterprise services.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Testing becomes more extensive and integration-focused because orchestrated pipelines depend on reliable interactions, automated sequencing, trigger behavior, and coherent end-to-end execution across multiple services.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity

impacts.justification: Provide user support is the third strongest relationship because the role responds to requests from subject-matter specialists, clients, managers, employees and the general public; explains data availability, consistency, methods and techniques; and interprets user requests for custom tabulations. Future drivers such as AI chatbots, metadata-driven discoverability, self-service platforms, and workforce efficiency pressures are likely to shift this work toward more digital self-service support, FAQ/knowledge-base use, and support for more complex questions about methods, quality and confidentiality.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity

impacts.justification: The strongest relationship is with Design collection because the role evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results; prepares operational specifications and training for manual and automated collection; recommends procedures, software and hardware for collection; and works with data suppliers or respondents to explain data formatting and statistical concepts. This is stronger than adjacent subprocesses because the evidence points to determining and refining collection methods and operational specifications, not merely running existing collection. Future drivers such as administrative and alternative data expansion, online-first collection, secure digital collection, and enterprise platforms will materially change this work toward digital acquisition, supplier coordination, API-based collection and more adaptive collection design, increasing skill needs in digital collection architecture and secure source integration.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production

Workforce impacts are strong because collection staff roles shift from traditional field operations toward digital collection, supplier coordination and source monitoring.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity

impacts.justification: Prepare and submit business case is the second strongest relationship because the role prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impacts of new or modified programs, and defines and evaluates the cost of system development work. This is stronger than generic need-identification subprocesses because the role is involved in concrete proposals for program and systems change, not just environmental scanning. Future drivers such as cost realignment, governance discipline, platform modernization and workforce skills transition will increase the importance of structured proposals that justify strategic production-system choices under constraint.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Business cases are materially reshaped by AI and automation because proposed production models now explicitly compare manual versus automated workflows, shared enterprise solutions, workforce upskilling needs, governance controls, and expected gains in speed, repeatability, and reduced duplication.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Business cases are materially reshaped to justify replacing or supplementing surveys with administrative, alternative and linked data, including investments in linkage infrastructure, source agreements, online-first collection residuals, and workforce training. Cost-benefit and risk assessments increasingly compare survey burden reduction and timeliness gains against integration complexity, source dependency and skills requirements.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production

impacts.justification: The strongest relationship is to creating frame and selecting sample because the work directly involves validation of collection unit boundaries, refinement of collection units, delineation of assignments for collection managers and staff, identification of operationally mailable areas, and resolution of geocoding, boundary issues and collection unit types. Those activities are operational frame-instantiation and area delineation work for census collection. This is stronger than design subprocesses because the description is about applying and validating the frame for the iteration of collection, not designing the methodology. Future drivers around administrative, linked and geospatial data expansion may materially change this work by increasing use of richer geospatial and register inputs for frame creation, boundary validation and selective targeting.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Operational frame creation is materially affected because frames are increasingly instantiated from administrative registers and linked sources, with more use of census-style extraction and more targeted residual sampling. Auxiliary variables from non-survey sources also become more important for sample coordination and burden management.

impacts.justification: The second strongest relationship is to running collection because the role supports live census operations through daily analysis of management information reports, recommendations to management to resolve anomalies, tactical strategies for collective dwelling collection, support to census field offices, and interpretation of directives to address collection requirements in difficult areas. This reflects direct operational involvement in monitoring and adjusting collection execution. It is stronger than 4.2 because the emphasis is on active support during planning and collection phases and on resolving live operational issues. Future drivers tied to agility, digital collection, adaptive collection and integrated operational monitoring are likely to increase the need for real-time analysis, anomaly detection, and targeted collection interventions.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Collection execution is fundamentally changed by the shift toward scheduled receipt, extraction and monitoring of administrative, alternative and open data, combined with online-first survey operations and adaptive follow-up. Workforce impacts are substantial because collection workload shifts in nature, not just volume.

drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because the driver explicitly emphasizes operating to deadlines, milestone management, and active execution. Collection operations must be monitored closely, adjusted quickly, and managed against time-bound targets while maintaining sufficient quality and stewardship.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure

This subprocess becomes more effective and more central because source suitability, interoperability, reuse potential, and accompanying metadata quality can be evaluated systematically rather than through ad hoc source-by-source investigation.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: This driver materially shifts this subprocess toward systematic assessment of administrative and alternative data as primary or complementary inputs to modernized statistical programs. Suitability reviews must now account for linked data environments, unstructured-source extraction, integrated pipelines, and enterprise-scale production feasibility, not just traditional survey-source fitness.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Efficiency and cost pressures strongly increase the importance of finding lower-cost data sources and collection substitutes, especially administrative and other reusable sources that reduce direct collection burden and staffing needs.

impacts.justification: This subprocess is material because the role recommends and implements new methods of processing, modeling, analyzing and disseminating data. Evidence includes: 'implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data' and 'provides specialized technical, advisory and consultative services.' That aligns with designing processing and analysis methodologies, especially for integrated, linked and alternative data environments. It is stronger than dissemination-only subprocesses because the emphasis is on methods and technical initiatives rather than product assembly. Future drivers such as AI and automation, modern statistical methods and integrated pipelines will shift the role toward more advanced model-based processing, automated validation/integration logic, and stronger method governance and reproducibility skills.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: This subprocess is directly transformed by AI and automation because coding, validation, editing, imputation, integration, and some analytical routines are redesigned around AI-enabled and automated methods, with added requirements for quality assurance, transparency, governance, and reproducibility.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Processing and analysis design is heavily affected because the driver requires methodologies for integrating multiple administrative and alternative sources, record linkage, source prioritisation, validation across heterogeneous inputs, and estimation under reduced direct collection. It also increases the need to design methods for unstructured and geospatial data handling and for quality assessment of linked-source outputs.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Processing and analysis design is directly affected because privacy protection and confidentiality controls must be built into integration, validation and output preparation methods. The driver also increases the need to design secure handling patterns for sensitive linked data and process-specific disclosure control.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Processing and analysis design is materially affected because enterprise data platforms and centralized repositories change how integration, validation and disclosure-control methods are operationalized. Design increasingly assumes scalable cloud execution environments, standardized data pipelines and stronger embedded security/privacy controls.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Processing and analysis design is strongly affected because methods must be specified as orchestratable, automatable pipeline steps with clear sequencing, dependencies, triggers, and exception paths across integrated production flows.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Metadata-driven management significantly affects processing and analysis design because integration, validation, coding and transformation rules increasingly rely on standardized metadata definitions. Processing design must account for metadata as an operational input, not just documentation.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: This is one of the most directly affected subprocesses because the driver is fundamentally about modernizing statistical methods and production models. Method design must now incorporate AI-enabled coding, advanced estimation, linkage-based integration, alternative-data processing, adaptive validation, and streamlined automated workflows to improve quality and timeliness.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: Processing and analysis design is materially reshaped toward modular, reusable processing components and standard validation patterns. Methods and rules increasingly need to be expressed in forms that can be deployed through shared services or self-service platforms while remaining governed, supportable, and production-ready.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Processing and analysis methods are redesigned to substitute automation and model-based methods for manual effort, especially in coding, validation, editing, imputation, and integration workflows.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because modernization depends on staff being able to design and govern new methods using AI, advanced analytical tools, open-source technologies, and new data sources. Method design must reflect current and planned workforce capability, training needs, and leadership oversight for methodological change.

impacts.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role is fundamentally about preparing, validating, storing, linking and disseminating statistical metadata. Evidence includes: 'plans... the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata,' 'directs the development of... documentation, procedures manuals and training materials... related to the production, storage dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata,' and repeated references to production, storage and dissemination of metadata. This maps directly to updating output systems where data and metadata are formatted, loaded and linked for dissemination. It is stronger than other subprocesses because dissemination-ready metadata storage and linkage are explicit responsibilities, not adjacent implications. Future drivers around metadata-driven discoverability, enterprise platforms and reusable dissemination systems will likely increase demand for standardized metadata structures, stronger linkage to dissemination repositories, and platform-based metadata governance skills.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Updating output systems is materially affected because automated dissemination pipelines and enterprise platforms increase the importance of standardized loading, metadata linkage, and controlled system updates for scalable release operations.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Output systems are materially affected because dissemination databases must store and expose richer metadata about source composition, linkage, quality and geospatial content. The driver also increases the need to maintain explicit links between outputs and methodological metadata for mixed-source products.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Output systems are materially affected because dissemination-ready stores must be securely updated and managed, with metadata and data linked in ways that preserve confidentiality and support controlled access. This is especially important for modern digital dissemination platforms.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Updating output systems is materially affected because dissemination repositories are increasingly enterprise platforms or cloud-hosted systems that require standardized loading, metadata linkage, access controls and scalable storage patterns.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because dissemination systems become downstream nodes in integrated pipelines, receiving automated data and metadata loads from prior stages with minimal manual intervention.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: This subprocess is directly and strongly affected because the driver is fundamentally about metadata-rich, searchable, standardized assets. Updating output systems must ensure metadata are formatted, loaded, linked and ready to support discovery and reuse.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: Output system updates are materially affected because modular dissemination architectures rely on interoperable services, shared metadata components, and standard loading patterns. This shifts work toward governed configuration and integration of reusable output services.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: This subprocess is affected through increased emphasis on automated loading and standardized metadata handling to reduce recurring operational effort.

impacts.justification: This subprocess is highly relevant because metadata quality evaluation is a central and repeated responsibility. Evidence includes: 'plans, directs and undertakes quality evaluations,' 'reviews and certifies the results of quality evaluations,' 'compiles results and writes reports,' and 'analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality... reviews the comparability of metadata over time... provides management with reports of findings.' This aligns directly with conducting evaluation by synthesizing evidence, assessing quality issues and recommending changes. It is ranked below 7.1 because the role spans the full metadata lifecycle, but evaluation is still a core owned responsibility rather than incidental. Future drivers such as governance, prioritization, operational efficiency and metadata-driven management will increase continuous evaluation expectations, dashboard-style reporting, reuse metrics and more formal recommendations on metadata quality and enterprise consistency.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially transformed because AI and automation make continuous performance dashboards, quality benchmarking, and rapid improvement cycles more feasible, while also requiring explicit assessment of trust, transparency, workforce readiness, and governance effectiveness.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially affected because success criteria now include burden reduction, timeliness gains, source stability, linkage quality, online-first performance and workforce readiness. Reports must assess whether expanded use of administrative and linked data actually improved relevance and efficiency without unacceptable quality or operational risks.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because the driver makes schedule performance, milestone attainment, execution discipline, and implementation effectiveness central evaluation criteria. Evaluation becomes more operational, dashboard-driven, and oriented to rapid corrective action and future delivery improvement.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Evaluation itself is materially affected because process success must now be judged partly on security, privacy, secure-access and resilience outcomes, not only statistical quality and efficiency. Recommendations for future iterations will therefore increasingly target secure modernization gaps.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially affected because enterprise digital platforms provide richer operational dashboards and performance evidence on system readiness, security, scalability and workflow efficiency, allowing more continuous assessment of platform-enabled production processes.

drivers.driver: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially affected because stronger governance and prioritization increase the importance of evidence-based performance assessment, explicit comparison against priorities, and disciplined recommendations about what should be improved, scaled, deferred or stopped.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially affected because performance assessment increasingly focuses on end-to-end flow efficiency, automation effectiveness, exception rates, and orchestration reliability rather than isolated step performance.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially affected because success criteria increasingly include whether assets are discoverable, metadata-complete, interoperable and reused. This changes what performance is assessed and what improvements are recommended.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially affected because modernization requires explicit assessment of whether new methods, platforms, and production models are delivering expected gains in quality, timeliness, efficiency, and respondent burden reduction. Continuous evaluation becomes more important in enterprise transformation.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: Evaluation is materially affected because the success of modular architecture and self-service development must be assessed in terms of reuse, interoperability, governance compliance, support burden, validation outcomes, and sustainability of delivery.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: This subprocess is directly affected because operational efficiency and cost realignment require systematic evaluation of productivity, savings, automation benefits, service impacts, and whether processes should be redesigned, scaled back, or stopped.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: Evaluation is strongly affected because modernization success depends not only on statistical quality but also on workforce readiness, leadership effectiveness, training uptake, adoption of new tools, and sustainability under staffing reductions. These become core dimensions of process evaluation and improvement recommendations.

impacts.justification: This subprocess is also materially supported because the role gathers, analyzes and compiles inputs used for metadata quality assessment. Evidence includes: 'evaluates and investigates... metadata requirements,' 'compiles results,' 'analyses client requirements,' and 'analyses current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods.' While the role goes beyond gathering inputs into full evaluation, there is clear responsibility for assembling evidence and quality information. It is ranked below 8.2 because the description more strongly emphasizes analysis, certification and reporting than collection of inputs alone. Future drivers will likely increase the continuous capture of metadata quality indicators, repository usage signals, standards compliance metrics and system-generated evidence to support enterprise metadata evaluation.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is strongly affected because AI-enabled and automated production generates richer system metrics, paradata, and monitoring outputs that can be collected continuously to assess workflow performance, quality, and adoption impacts.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Evaluation inputs are materially affected because the organisation must gather new indicators on source quality, linkage performance, online response behaviour, adaptive collection effectiveness, workload shifts and user reactions to mixed-source outputs. Staff feedback on tools and training also becomes more important.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline
drivers.impact: This subprocess is materially affected because execution discipline increases the importance of collecting evidence on milestone performance, schedule adherence, bottlenecks, and barrier removal. Evaluation inputs must support active management and future acceleration of delivery.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is materially affected because cyber, privacy and secure-access performance indicators become important evidence for assessing modernized statistical processes. Security-related system metrics and access-control evidence need to be captured alongside traditional quality indicators.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is materially affected because enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure make system metrics, paradata and workflow telemetry more available and easier to centralize, enabling more continuous and automated evaluation.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is affected because integrated pipelines and orchestration generate richer continuous process metadata, system metrics, and flow-status information across the full production chain.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is materially affected because metadata-driven operations generate richer process metadata, usage signals and quality indicators that can be used to assess discoverability, reuse and interoperability outcomes.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is materially affected because modernized production generates richer process metadata, paradata, system metrics, and staff feedback from automated and integrated workflows. These inputs become essential for assessing whether modernization is improving quality, timeliness, and efficiency.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is materially affected because modular platforms and reusable services generate standardised operational metrics, validation results, and component-level performance information that are important for governing self-service development and sustaining reusable assets.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering becomes more important as efficiency programs require evidence on savings, productivity, service trade-offs, and workforce impacts, with stronger reliance on automated process metrics.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: Evaluation input gathering is materially affected because workforce transition requires systematic capture of staff feedback, training outcomes, workflow issues, and adoption metrics alongside standard process indicators to assess modernization readiness and sustainability.

impacts.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role analyzes user requirements from other national statistical offices and determines appropriate sources of information, methods and approaches. Evidence includes: 'Analyzes the user requirements for data users of other national statistical offices... determines... which sources of information, methods and approaches should be used' and 'Analysis is required to understand and interpret requests for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request.' This aligns most directly with checking data availability and suitability, especially where requests, sources and delivery approaches must be assessed. It is stronger than dissemination subprocesses because the role first determines what information can be provided and by what sources/methods before coordinating delivery. Future drivers such as administrative and alternative data expansion, secure access and enterprise platforms may reshape this work by increasing cross-country source options, data-sharing constraints, and the need to assess feasibility of new data forms and delivery mechanisms.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: AI and automation materially change source assessment by making unstructured and machine-readable sources more usable for statistical purposes, while increasing the importance of assessing cloud, security, governance, monitoring, and workflow integration requirements before adoption.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: This driver directly shifts source strategy from survey-first to systematic assessment of administrative, alternative, linked and unstructured sources. The subprocess is materially expanded to evaluate SDLE-enabled linkage opportunities, suitability of administrative and alternative data, geospatial/gridded inputs, access conditions, continuity, metadata quality, and residual survey gaps. Workforce impacts are significant because staff need tools and training to assess non-survey sources and manage increased cross-program source acquisition during parallel agency operations.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Security, privacy and secure-access requirements materially change how data sources are assessed for suitability, especially for administrative and external data. Source selection, access conditions, legal agreements, storage approaches and platform choices must now explicitly account for cyber risk, privacy constraints, authorization models and operational resilience before a source can be considered viable.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Enterprise cloud and platform modernization materially changes how data source options are assessed by making scalable storage, centralized repositories, secure access, privacy controls and modern ingestion tooling core feasibility criteria. It increases the viability of using larger and more diverse administrative and external sources, while also requiring explicit assessment of cyber security, authorizations and cloud-based access conditions.

drivers.driver: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline
drivers.impact: Governance and prioritization materially affect how data source options are assessed by emphasizing enterprise-level trade-offs, clearer accountability for source choices, and disciplined selection of sources that best support highest-value outcomes under resource constraints.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Searchable, standardized, metadata-rich repositories materially change how existing data sources are discovered and assessed. This subprocess becomes more effective and more central because source suitability, interoperability, reuse potential, and accompanying metadata quality can be evaluated systematically rather than through ad hoc source-by-source investigation.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: This driver materially shifts this subprocess toward systematic assessment of administrative and alternative data as primary or complementary inputs to modernized statistical programs. Suitability reviews must now account for linked data environments, unstructured-source extraction, integrated pipelines, and enterprise-scale production feasibility, not just traditional survey-source fitness.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Efficiency and cost pressures strongly increase the importance of finding lower-cost data sources and collection substitutes, especially administrative and other reusable sources that reduce direct collection burden and staffing needs.

impacts.justification: This subprocess is strongly relevant because the role coordinates delivery of data and information to international organizations and ensures approvals before release. Evidence includes: 'Coordinates the delivery of data and information,' 'negotiates for deadline extensions or staggered delivery where appropriate,' and 'ensures that all necessary approvals are secured prior to delivery.' This directly matches managing release timing, approvals and controlled provision to external users. It is ranked below 1.5 because delivery/release follows from the prior assessment and coordination of requests, but it is still materially part of the work. Future drivers around execution discipline, secure access and digital platforms will likely increase emphasis on release governance, deadline control, secure external delivery and possible controlled access arrangements for international stakeholders.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Release activities are affected where expanded linked and administrative data use changes briefing content, access arrangements for confidential microdata, and communication around methodological change. The impact is real but less direct than in source, design and processing subprocesses.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline
drivers.impact: This subprocess is one of the most directly affected because the driver explicitly concerns timelines, milestones, and execution discipline. Release management must operate to fixed schedules with strong coordination, clear authority, active risk management, and disciplined contingency handling.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Release is directly affected because secure access for authorized users, embargo handling, controlled provision of confidential data and resilient release operations are central concerns under this driver. This subprocess operationalizes secure dissemination and restricted-access release.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Release processes are materially affected because cloud-based dissemination channels, enterprise platforms and controlled-access environments change how products are released, accessed and governed, especially for authorized users and confidential data.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Release management is materially affected because orchestrated pipelines can automate release readiness, timing, and downstream publication actions while preserving controlled approval and exception paths.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Release is materially affected because metadata completeness and linkage are now part of what must be in place for a successful release. Access to products, especially reusable data assets and confidential products, depends on accurate metadata and discoverability controls.

impacts.justification: This subprocess is meaningfully related because the role gathers and analyzes international user needs and emerging issues to shape comparative studies and internal mobilization. Evidence includes: 'gathers, compiles, analyzes and interprets information and data requests from multilateral organizations,' 'researches and provides more background and supporting information for new or emerging topics,' and 'conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices in order to recommend areas of improvement.' This fits identifying needs, especially from external users and environmental changes. It is ranked below 1.5 and 7.3 because the job appears to respond to and coordinate needs rather than formally set corporate output objectives. Future drivers such as governance, prioritization and modern methods may increase demand for more disciplined triage of international requests and sharper assessment of which emerging global topics warrant Statistics Canada engagement.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Fiscal constraint and cost realignment directly change which statistical needs can be pursued, requiring stronger triage of programs, reconsideration of service levels, and identification of opportunities to replace labour-intensive approaches with more efficient methods.

impacts.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the position directly manages live collection operations. Evidence includes: 'manages the work of the district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities,' 'develops and implements long term strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes,' and 'resolves complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents.' This maps directly to running collection, including respondent contact, monitoring, adjustment and closure against operational targets. It is stronger than adjacent collection subprocesses because the description emphasizes day-to-day execution, response patterns, respondent behaviour, productivity and operational control. Future drivers such as online-first collection, AI-enabled support, adaptive collection, cost pressures and secure digital channels will materially change this work toward more digitally managed, monitored and targeted collection with fewer purely manual interventions.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Running collection is directly transformed by AI and automation through chatbot-supported respondent interactions, automated follow-up and intake, machine-readable/open-data acquisition, real-time monitoring, and reduced manual intervention in operational collection activities.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Collection execution is fundamentally changed by the shift toward scheduled receipt, extraction and monitoring of administrative, alternative and open data, combined with online-first survey operations and adaptive follow-up. The subprocess increasingly manages supplier interactions, machine-readable feeds, and dynamic collection adjustments rather than only respondent contact. Workforce impacts are substantial because collection workload shifts in nature, not just volume.

drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because the driver explicitly emphasizes operating to deadlines, milestone management, and active execution. Collection operations must be monitored closely, adjusted quickly, and managed against time-bound targets while maintaining sufficient quality and stewardship.

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Live collection is materially affected because data gathering, respondent interactions, supplier transfers and monitoring must operate through secure channels with privacy protections in place. As digital collection expands, cyber resilience and controlled access become operational requirements during execution, not just design considerations.

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
drivers.impact: Running collection is materially affected because enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure support digital collection operations, monitoring, respondent interactions and fieldwork coordination, while secure access and cyber protections become operational requirements during live collection.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
drivers.impact: Collection operations are materially affected where incoming data and metadata are expected to flow automatically into downstream stages, with more real-time monitoring of collection status and fewer manual transfer points.

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Running collection is materially affected because metadata must be gathered, checked and monitored as part of operational collection. The driver increases the importance of collecting associated metadata reliably so assets remain discoverable and reusable after ingestion.

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production
drivers.impact: Collection execution is materially transformed by adaptive collection, online-first operations, chatbot-enabled respondent support, and increased use of administrative and alternative data feeds. It also changes how field activities are coordinated and how collection is monitored and adjusted in real time to improve quality and efficiency.

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
drivers.impact: Operational efficiency pressures change how collection is run by increasing reliance on lower-touch digital collection, automated monitoring, and reduced manual follow-up and field effort where feasible.

drivers.driver: Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity
drivers.impact: Running collection is materially affected because staff must operate new digital collection tools and methods while maintaining respondent relationships and quality under workforce adjustment pressures. Managerial support and communication capability become important to sustain performance during transition.

impacts.justification: This subprocess is also central because the role ensures operational readiness of people, systems and procedures before and during collection cycles. Evidence includes: 'manages... planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities,' 'manages the recruitment, development and retention, of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce,' and 'establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.' This aligns directly with setting up collection, including staffing, training, technology readiness and confidentiality procedures. It is ranked below 4.3 because the position is more explicitly accountable for running ongoing collection than for one-time setup alone, but setup responsibilities are still material. Future drivers will likely increase the role's focus on digital platform readiness, secure credentialing, staff reskilling for new tools, and scalable preparation for mixed-mode and source-based collection.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
drivers.impact: Collection setup is strongly affected because AI-enabled collection requires new staff training, system preparation, secure configuration of digital tools and APIs, readiness of automated extraction and chatbot channels, and operational preparation for embedded workflow execution.

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
drivers.impact: Collection setup is strongly affected because readiness now includes source acquisition arrangements, secure receipt/extraction of administrative and alternative data, online-first respondent setup, prefill, APIs, and staff training for mixed-source operations. drivers.driver: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability

drivers.driver: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
